novelty_flags.label: Proposition 6 and related_work comparison to arXiv:2201.06898v1
novelty_flags.one_line: The cited Theorem 3 identifies delta_1, an unweighted average of individual slopes, not the proposal's WAOSS formula; move the WAOSS nesting derivation to the proposal's own result or compare it to the appropriate published weighted result.

novelty_flags.label: Proposition 11 (common-baseline reduction)
novelty_flags.one_line: The claimed scalar bounded-CAS interval is already the sharp WAS result of deChaisemartinCicciaDHaultfoeuilleKnau2024HeterogeneousAdoptionV4, Theorem 4; retain it only as a sanity reduction, not a novelty-bearing result.

soundness_flags.label: ass:conditional-parallel-trends
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited proceedings assumption quantifies doses over the baseline-treatment support D1, whereas this condition quantifies every d in the larger declared interval I; narrow it to the source domain or retag and justify the stronger all-I condition as novel.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 4 (point identification)
soundness_flags.one_line: Because A_P is defined as the closed span of differences of obstacle-admissible functions, constancy of J_P over C_P is exactly annihilation of A_P; the advertised criterion presently unfolds its own definition.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 1 (full-law sharpness)
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Sharpness is only over completions with continuous globally L-Lipschitz baseline trends and the new conditional mean-movement bound.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The identified set is sharp conditional on that explicitly delimited completion subclass and mean-movement restriction.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 12 and Proposition 13
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Uniform inference is restricted to the known finite-rectangle, fixed-Holder, bounded-density, bounded-outcome, denominator-separated class.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The outer-coverage claim is conditional on membership in P_reg and is not a claim of adaptive or unknown-support inference.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 610, Assumptions 2-4; p. 611, Theorem 1; p. 613, proof lines immediately before and at display (4)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Assumption 2 is stated for every d in the baseline-treatment support D1, Assumption 4 states only marginal Pr(|Delta D|<=eta)>0, and the proof asserts Pr(|Delta D|<=eta|D1)>0 before defining the conditional mean.

Assumption 5 states Supp(D1|M_delta=1) subset Supp(D1|M_delta=0), equivalently P(M_delta=1|D1)<1 a.s.; Theorem 3 identifies delta_1 through E[(Y2-Y1-lim_delta->0 E[Y2-Y1|D1,M_delta=0])/(D2-D1)|M=1], rather than the WAOSS functional.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 23, Design 1 and Assumption 4; Theorem 4; Appendix B.2, p. 45
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: For the common-baseline Design 1 with D1=0 and D2>0, Theorem 4 gives sharp upper and lower WAS bounds under bounded conditional average slopes.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the circular A_P definition with an independently computable dual, kernel, or finite-program characterization; otherwise demote the annihilator statement to a corollary of interval constancy.
Repair the source chain by separating the v1 delta_1 comparison from the WAOSS nesting claim, and state exactly which published weighted theorem is recovered under conditional quasi-stayer support.

State the all-I parallel-trends restriction as a genuinely new assumption with an application-level justification, or narrow it to the source's baseline-support domain and redo the completion argument under that weaker scope.

recommended_next_step: Revise the source comparison and all-dose assumption, remove or independently characterize the definitional annihilator headline, then advance the retained full-law sharpness and uniform-inference kernel to Stage 0.
